celan: va karethaen unar thal del dren.
intent: Use half the water.
context: One identified supply of water.
reason: Thal supplies out of; treating the two as equal shares of the whole is the explicit new convention needed.

celan: va karethaen unar thal quen dren.
intent: Use a quarter of the water.
context: Same whole, four equal shares.
reason: Same structure scales without adding a word for quarter.

celan: va karethaen tren thal quen dren.
intent: Use three quarters of the water.
context: Same whole, four equal shares.
reason: The numerator selects three shares; the denominator fixes four equal shares.

celan: va karethaen unar thal del dren.
intent: Use half the combined water.
context: Two containers hold unequal quantities.
result: Fails if interpreted as choose one container
reason: One of two containers need not contain half the total. The fraction must describe equal abstract shares, not count existing containers.

celan: va karethaen unar thal verin dren.
intent: Use one zeroth of the water.
context: Denominator zero.
reason: No division into zero equal shares is defined.

celan: va karethaen peth thal quen dren.
intent: Use five quarters of the water.
context: Only one bounded supply is available.
reason: Five quarters is mathematically meaningful but cannot be taken from one whole supply. Distinguish a reference unit from the entire available stock.

celan: va var shan vorkor «tren».
intent: Go through door labelled three.
context: Doors have visible number labels.
reason: The quoted number identifies the label; no ordinal suffix or new meaning is needed.

celan: va var shan vorkor «tren».
intent: Go through the third door encountered.
context: Unlabelled doors; walking direction not stated.
result: Does not establish a general ordinal
reason: The label construction alone supplies neither counting direction nor a starting point.

celan: va var shan vorkor «tren».
intent: Go through the third door counted from the agreed start.
context: Speaker and listener first number the doors together.
reason: The earlier counting supplies the order. This is a contextual solution, not a universal ordinal rule.

celan: va tal emilpral «del» var I.
intent: Give me plate labelled two.
context: Plates are numbered for a task.
reason: Repeats the label strategy with another noun; does not mean give me two plates.

celan: rinaen peth shen morlak worlian.
intent: Five measures of grain are enough.
context: Preparing a meal with a shared measure.
reason: Worlian already appears as a predicate. This states sufficiency, not an exact minimum.

celan: rinaen peth shen morlak worlian. ver rinaen quen shen morlak worlian.
intent: Five measures suffice; four do not.
context: Only whole measures are offered; larger supplies are useful.
reason: Gives a practical threshold in this scenario. It does not resolve every quantity between four and five or independently promise that excess is acceptable.

celan: peth reth ther peth
intent: Five or more.
context: An amount expression.
reason: Reth and Ther have the right semantic ingredients, but current Ther syntax compares a stated quality: X adjective Ther Y. A bare-number comparison must be explicitly established.

celan: rinaen peth shen morlak worlian. ver rinaen quen shen morlak worlian.
intent: The minimum is exactly five.
context: 4.5 measures are possible.
result: Insufficient for an exact lower bound
reason: The clauses leave 4.5 unsettled. Do not label this wording an exact at-least construction.

celan: va tal peth shen morlak var I.
intent: Give me the same amount as the other recipient.
context: The other recipient received five of the same measure of grain.
result: Works by repeating the known quantity
reason: Numerical equality is communicated without a separate same word, provided the measure is shared.

celan: va tal unar shen morlak var Ya. va tal unar shen morlak var I.
intent: Give us equal amounts.
context: One calibrated measure is used for both recipients.
reason: Two equal unit amounts establish equality operationally, without Thaleth.

celan: va tal shen denya var I.
intent: Give me the same amount as that.
context: The listener indicates a reference measure.
reason: May request the measure itself or a measured quantity matching it. Use a named material and explicit count when precision matters.

celan: va tal shenlian var I.
intent: Give me the same amount.
context: No shared reference amount.
result: Does not preserve the instruction reliably
reason: Shenlian names a standard/reference measure, not equality to an unnamed earlier quantity.

celan: rinaen peth shen morlak-ka belshen peth shena.
intent: The total price of five measures of grain is five coins.
context: One agreed measure and one understood currency.
reason: Read the possessor as the full phrase five measures of grain. No new price word is required; the phrase boundary should be taught explicitly.

celan: rinaen unar shen morlak-ka belshen del shena.
intent: One measure of grain costs two coins.
context: Same market convention.
reason: Changes quantity and price independently, so the example does not depend on both numbers being five.

celan: rinaen peth shen morlak-ka belshen peth shena.
intent: Each of five measures costs five coins.
context: Seller intends a total of twenty-five coins.
reason: The proposed wording states the price for the five-measure lot, not five coins per individual measure.

celan: rinaen peth shen morlak-ka belshen peth shena.
intent: A fully specified price independent of market context.
context: Different measuring vessels or currencies are possible.
result: Needs the unit and currency clarified
reason: Coin type and measure must be shared or specified. This is a missing reference, not necessarily missing grammar. Counted Shena versus Shenan remains a separate teaching decision.
